slides.title: [Sentence] / window / retrieval
slides.hook: Sentence windows ignore headings and overlap: at top_k=4, they sent more text than the whole handbook.
inside: A run where the next sentence held the answer
When to pick it over parent-document

slides.title: One sentence in, / a [window] out
slides.text: LlamaIndex (`llama-index-core` 0.14.25) builds it from two pieces:

steps: `SentenceWindowNodeParser` splits each document into sentences with NLTK's Punkt tokenizer: one node per sentence.
Each node keeps its neighbors in `metadata["window"]`: `window_size=3` sentences on each side by default.
Only the sentence is embedded; `window` and `original_text` are excluded.
At query time, `MetadataReplacementPostProcessor` swaps each hit's text for its window.

slides.title: The next sentence / held the [answer]
slides.text: A 1,360-character support handbook, split into 27 sentence nodes. Query: "Who has to approve refunds over $500?"

visuals.label: Top hit (spaCy en_core_web_md vectors)

chunks.text: Refunds over $500 follow a separate rule.

visuals.verdict: The sentence alone doesn't say who approves

visuals.label: Its window, window_size=3: 363 characters
chunks: … Refunds go back to the original payment method. Refunds over $500 follow a separate rule. !!They need a second approval from the finance team.!! Finance replies within 2 business days. …
visuals.verdict: The answer comes back with the window

slides.title: The window needs / a [postprocessor]
slides.text: The parser only stores the window. Same query, retriever without `MetadataReplacementPostProcessor`:

visuals.code:
hit = retriever.retrieve(q)[0]
hit.node.text
# {{'Refunds over $500 follow a separate rule. '}}
len(hit.node.metadata["window"])
# 363

bullets: The window is also excluded from the LLM's view of metadata, so the model gets the bare sentence.
Pass the postprocessor in `node_postprocessors` on the query engine, with `target_metadata_key="window"`.

slides.title: Windows [cross] / headings
slides.text: A window stops only at the edge of the document or node it was built from. Query: "Do international orders pay customs fees?"

visuals.label: Whole handbook as one Document
chunks: … International orders pay customs fees on delivery. Tracking links are emailed when the order ships. Damaged parcels are replaced at no cost … !!## Warranty Every device has a 1-year warranty from the delivery date.!!
visuals.verdict: A Shipping hit carries a Warranty sentence

visuals.label: MarkdownNodeParser first, then the window parser
chunks: … International orders pay customs fees on delivery. Tracking links are emailed when the order ships. !!Damaged parcels are replaced at no cost when the customer sends a photo within 7 days.!!
visuals.verdict: The window ends with the Shipping section

slides.title: Nearby hits / [repeat] lines
slides.text: Windows aren't merged. Query: "How long do warranty repairs take?", `similarity_top_k=4`:
bullets: The windows around sentences 15, 18 and 20 overlap, so sentence 18 reaches the model 3 times.
Drop a hit whose sentence already sits in a higher-ranked window. Here: 3 windows, 1,066 characters, answer kept.

slides.title: Size the window / in [sentences]
slides.text: `window_size` counts sentences on each side, so the characters follow sentence length. The refund query's top hit:
slides.after: Here 1 was enough. Test sizes on your own questions: when the answer is the next sentence, a bigger window adds tokens and no facts.

slides.title: Every node stores / its [window]
slides.text: Each sentence node carries its whole window in `metadata`, and the docstore saves every node with it. The 1,360-character handbook:
bullets: At size 3, the stored windows are 6.6 times the text itself.
The vector count stays at 27; the extra characters land in the docstore.

slides.title: Put it all / [together]

visuals.code:
pipeline = IngestionPipeline(
    transformations=[
        MarkdownNodeParser(),
        SentenceWindowNodeParser
            .from_defaults(window_size=2)])
index = VectorStoreIndex(
    pipeline.run(documents=docs))
engine = index.as_query_engine(
    similarity_top_k=4,
    node_postprocessors=[
        MetadataReplacementPostProcessor(
            target_metadata_key="window")])

bullets: Drop overlapping hits before the prompt is built.

cards.title: Use it when
items: One or two sentences hold the answer: policies, specs, FAQs
Facts lean on the sentence before or after
The text is prose that splits cleanly into sentences

cards.title: Move on when
items: Answers need a whole section's steps or structure: use the parent-document retriever
The text is tables, code or lists, where a sentence is a poor unit
Storage per node matters: each one keeps its window

slides.title: [Cheat] sheet
rows: Embed one sentence, return its neighbors
Add `MetadataReplacementPostProcessor`, or the model sees one sentence
Split on headings first, or windows cross sections
Drop hits already inside a higher-ranked window
Each node stores its window: plan the storage

slides.line: Sentence splitting assumes prose. For source code, the unit to keep whole is the function, signature and body together.
